categories._data_note: Rows matched via consistent name-order across all 7 screenshots (confirmed via the highlighted Muratec Motorum Hybrid 2558 2000W row appearing at position 18 in images 4-7). Image 3's Rates/Limits table appeared to have slightly fewer visible rows than the other tables (23 vs 26), so punch_rate/nibble_rate/rapid_traverse_rate/max_sheet_width/max_thickness values for a couple of Amada models (rows 5-6) carry a small risk of a 1-row misalignment - worth spot-checking Amada EML 3610 NT (4000W) against source if precision matters.

Source images were photos of a screen (moderate glare/blur). Row 11 (KMT SL-V 100 PLUS) had an ambiguous overhead-input reading in the source photo; installation/uptime/maintenance factors were normalized to the category's standard pattern (20/80/5) rather than the anomalous raw text.

Source images for this batch were photos of a monitor with visible glare/blur (unlike prior batches which were clean digital screenshots). Core fields (price, manufacturer, labor rate, bed/sheet dimensions, preferred flag, avg utilization) were legible and are high-confidence. Some secondary fields for a few rows near the bottom of the DO/IO and tooling tables (images 2,3,5) were harder to distinguish with certainty - these are included but flagged per-row where confidence is lower. Recommend a quick visual spot-check against the original tool if these machines feed into cost-critical calculations.

categories._data_note: Source images are photos of a monitor with visible glare/blur (not clean screenshots). Row identity and press_force_kn were cross-validated as identical and in the same order across all 4 source images, confirming no row misalignment. However, shut_height_mm was only clearly legible for the 5 'Progressive Die Press - X,000kN' rows and the 4 Aida SMX rows; for Schuler and United Power rows it is set to null because the visible digits were ambiguous with an adjacent column under glare and a fabricated value would be unreliable for costing. machine_power_kw is null for the 2 Schuler models (1150 Ton, A2/200-360) for the same reason. max_thickness_brass_mm, max_thickness_copper_mm and max_thickness_stainless_steel_mm were not distinctly legible per-row for Schuler/United Power/Niagara/Bliss (only max_thickness_aluminum_mm was confidently read) and are omitted pending source verification -- recommend confirming these against the original the system session if precision on thickness limits matters for costing.

Confirmed with user this table is the 'Tandem Press' process (images 2/4 labeled these rows 'Tandem Press - X,000kN Press Force'; images 6/7 read 'Standard Press' for the same rows under photo glare -- price/spec match confirmed identical rows, user selected Tandem Press as the correct name). Schuler 1150 Ton, Schuler A2/200-360, Schuler TSD 2000, and all 8 United Power SHD/SHS/THD variants are the same physical machines already captured in the 'Progressive Die Press' category with identical price/manufacturer -- their machine_length_mm/machine_width_mm/machine_power_kw/installation_factor_pct here were cross-validated against that category's clearer source images (8-11) rather than re-read from this batch's blurrier photos (images 1, 4, 7). machine_length_mm, machine_width_mm and machine_power_kw are null for 'Tandem Press - 1,500/3,000/5,000kN Press Force' because image 7 (a blurry phone photo, price-sorted so row-matched by machine_price_usd) was only confidently legible for the 7,000kN row; forcing values for the other three risked silent misreads -- recommend confirming against source if these fields matter.
